newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania shilling weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania shilling weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Tanzania shilling weakened against the dollar on Friday because of seasonal fluctuation, dealers said.
Against the dollar the shilling exchanged at a mean rate of 599.4450 compared to 599.3559 on Thursday. Last Friday it stood at 599.0985.

Against the pound the shilling stood at mean rate of 966.7879 from 969.8807 on Thursday. Trading on Tanzania's forex market is conducted almost entirely in dollars and dealers say as a result sterling transactions often do not reflect the larger forex trend.
Traders and financial analysts said they were unconcerned at the slight dollar depreciation which they attributed to "seasonal factors."
"As importers start to rebuild their inventories of imported goods following Christmas and (Moslem) Ramadan, demand for foreign exchange will go up," one dealer told Reuters.
"The price for forex goes up so the shilling goes down," said an analyst, adding that in the run up to June's budget the market would experience slight volatility.
"I suspect until budget time (June) there will be a tendency for speculative moves on the market by sellers and buyers," the analyst said."
The Bank of Tanzania had been active in the market selling dollars to meet importer demands, dealers said.

An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team is due to arrive in the capital this weekend to review Tanzania's economic performance prior to a second instalment of an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF).
The IMF agreed last November to an ESAF deal worth around $234 million over three years, the first IMF support for the country since 1992.
